Definition: from G303 and the base of G939; to go up (literally or figuratively):--arise, ascend (up), climb (go, grow, rise, spring) up, come (up).
BiblicalUsage: No man has ascended up to heaven, Jesus tells Nicodemus, but He that came down from heaven — and after the resurrection He tells Mary, 'I ascend unto my Father, and your Father.' Paul says when He ascended up on high He led captivity captive and gave gifts unto men, and John hears a voice like a trumpet say, 'Come up hither.' The word runs through the whole story of Christ: He came down, and He went up, and He will bring His people up after Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the going up is the proof of the coming down: He who descended is the same who ascended, and His ascension is my hope that where He is, I will be too. The gifts He gave when He ascended — apostles, prophets, teachers — are still the way He builds His church, and the voice that says 'Come up hither' is still the last word.
